text.text: <atomic>The drama program at our school has put on two plays this year, but we could do so much more. The problem is that the program doesn't get enough money and support to do its best.</atomic>
<atomic>If the school increased the drama program's budget, more students could participate, and our performances could be even more showstopping.</atomic>
<atomic>Drama teaches important life skills. Students learn public speaking, problem-solving, and creativity. These skills help in all subjects and prepare us for the future.</atomic>
<atomic>The drama program also helps students express themselves, build confidence, and work together as a team.</atomic>

<atomic>With more money, we could buy new props, repair lighting, and even invite local theater professionals to run workshops! This would make our program even more exciting and educational.</atomic>
<atomic>Some people might say that sports deserve a bigger budget because they bring school spirit and attract big crowds. But drama can do that, too!</atomic>
<atomic>A well-supported play can fill the auditorium and make our school proud.</atomic>
<atomic>Plus, not every student is an athlete. So, drama gives more students a chance to belong and succeed.</atomic>

<atomic>By investing in the drama program, our school would show that it values the arts just as much as athletics. We can make our next production the best one yet—if we get the support we deserve!</atomic>

textContent.text: Fantasy stories are filled with amazing imaginary creatures. Unicorns, elves, and goblins all burst from their pages. These magical beings are interesting, but the mighty dragon rules over them all.

pieces.text: Dragons are found in ancient tales from all over the world. In European legends, bold knights battle fierce, fiery dragons. In Chinese stories and myths, dragons bring rain and good fortune. Even today authors cannot resist writing about them. These creatures still appear in popular books and films
They have remained powerful and memorable creatures for centuries.

textContent.text: Dragons also come in many different forms. Some have wings, sharp claws, and fierce tempers. Some can breathe fire or control the weather. Depending on the story, dragons can be scary, helpful, clever, or wild. This wide range of traits makes them unpredictable and fun to meet.

Some readers may argue that unicorns, not dragons, are the most wonderful imaginary creatures. After all, unicorns are beautiful, and their horns are even said to heal sickness. But dragons can do so much more. They can drive a story's action by challenging heroes, protecting treasure, and even saving the day.
When it comes to imaginary creatures, there is no contest. The mighty dragon soars above the rest. It is the coolest imaginary creature of all!

textContent.text: We all love exciting stories, like a spaceship exploring the stars or a hero stepping into battle. While it can be fun to watch them, these stories can come to life without ever needing a screen. Movies can be exciting, but reading books is a better way to experience a story.

One reason a book is better than a movie is that you can move through a book at your own pace. When you read, you can stop to reflect on a scene and how it made you feel, or reread a certain part. Reading also fits easily into a busy schedule. Reading for five minutes here or there still keeps you connected to the story, making it the perfect hobby!

Books can also help the reader better understand the characters. Books often have more details about what the characters are thinking, not just what they say out loud. This helps you better understand a character's choices and feelings. Readers often feel deeply connected to characters in a personal way.

It's true that movies can be exciting, with colorful scenes and special effects. But books are even more powerful because they allow you to create those images in your own mind. When you read, you are the director. With the help of the author's description, you decide what the characters look like and how the world appears.
In the end, books offer a more individual experience than movies. That is why a book will always be better than a movie!

<atomic>Composting turns garbage into something good—and that's a change worth making for our community's future!</atomic>

textContent.text: Our community has a recycling program, and many of us walk to the store instead of driving. These small changes help our environment, but we can do more. Now, our community should consider composting.

Basically, composting means recycling food waste and yard scraps. Composting turns that waste into a natural fertilizer called compost. You can use it to feed all of your outdoor and indoor plants. Compost is less harmful to the environment than chemical fertilizers. And even better, it can save you a lot of money. No more trips to the garden store to buy plant food. Now you can make your own out of scraps you were going to throw away.

Reusing these waste materials means less garbage in landfills. This releases fewer harmful gasses into the atmosphere. Composting is a simple way our community can help the environment and make our gardens healthier at the same time. If more people composted, we'd have less trash, cleaner air, and better gardens all around town.

textContent.text: When it comes to kids and technology, the newest phones aren't always best. That's why we're asking parents at Rocky Middle School to hold off on giving students smartphones. Instead, consider basic phones for your kids.

Like a smartphone, a basic phone puts your child just a call or text away. This may be important to your family if your student is involved in after-school activities. It also helps them stay connected socially. They can call or text their friends to make plans or chat about school.

But the added benefit of basic phones is that they're not connected to the internet. They don't have games or social media. This makes them much less distracting than smartphones. This feature encourages students to stay focused on their classes and their friends.

Of course, there are many useful educational tools for smartphones. But while they can be beneficial for school improvement, they do not make a smartphone worthwhile. Your kids already have access to educational tools on their computers and tablets at school. We can also work with families to make sure that they can access these educational tools at home as needed. In other words, using educational tools does not require a smartphone.

Students at Rocky Middle School benefit from staying focused and connected. Basic phones can support that goal. That's why we'd like parents to consider basic phones for now. Smartphones might be better suited for high school.

They have remained powerful and memorable creatures for centuries.

textContent.text: Dragons also come in many different forms. Some have wings, sharp claws, and fierce tempers. Some can breathe fire or control the weather. Depending on the story, dragons can be scary, helpful, clever, or wild. This wide range of traits makes them unpredictable and fun to meet.

Some readers may argue that unicorns, not dragons, are the most wonderful imaginary creatures. After all, unicorns are beautiful, and their horns are even said to heal sickness. But dragons can do so much more. They can drive a story's action by challenging heroes, protecting treasure, and even saving the day.
When it comes to imaginary creatures, there is no contest. The mighty dragon soars above the rest. It is the coolest imaginary creature of all!
